# Draft:Mind the Gap: Scaling Businesses Across Cultures

----
Mind the Gap: Scaling Businesses Across Cultures is a business book by Vincent Lauria, Stefano Pellegrino, and Prof. Savanid (Nui) Vatanasakdakul, to be published by Wiley on May 4, 2026. The book draws on decades of cross-border business experience and academic research to offer frameworks for international business expansion, arguing that most failed expansions stem from cultural misunderstanding rather than poor strategy or insufficient capital.
Background
Vincent Lauria, after exiting his second Silicon Valley startup, spent a year traveling across Asia before settling in Singapore and co-founding Golden Gate Ventures in 2011. Over the following fifteen years of investing across more than 15 countries, he observed that cultural misalignment — not product weakness or capital constraints — was the primary driver of failed international expansions. Professor Savanid Vatanasakdakul of Carnegie Mellon University joined the project as academic contributor, grounding the book's frameworks in peer-reviewed Information Systems research.
Content
The book addresses market entry strategy, cross-border team management, and negotiation across cultural contexts. The authors introduce the concept of cultural code-switching — the adjustment of communication and behavioral styles when operating across different cultural environments — and illustrate how confident self-presentation may be interpreted as arrogance, direct communication as offensive, and apparent agreement as polite resistance.
Academic Contribution
Professor Vatanasakdakul's contribution is grounded in over 25 years of peer-reviewed research on digital transformation, socio-cultural technology adoption, and human-centric innovation. Her published work includes studies on enterprise resource planning adoption in China, IT governance frameworks, the role of culture in business-to-business technology adoption in Thailand, and the integration of ERP systems in accounting education. This body of research informs the book's treatment of how deeply embedded cultural logic — rather than bad faith or incompetence — underlies behaviors that can appear evasive or contradictory to outside observers.
Authors
Vincent Lauria is the Founding Partner of Golden Gate Ventures, a Singapore-based venture capital firm with over US$300 million in assets under management and more than 100 portfolio companies. He is a Kauffman Fellow and previously co-founded Meetro and Lefora in Silicon Valley.
Stefano Pellegrino is a three-time founder with a background in corporate law and cross-border mergers and acquisitions across Europe and Asia.
Savanid (Nui) Vatanasakdakul is a Full Teaching Professor of Information Systems at Carnegie Mellon University in Qatar. She holds a Ph.D. in Information Systems from the University of New South Wales, supported by the Australian Postgraduate Award Scholarship, and previously held a tenured position at Macquarie University for over a decade. She is the first Thai female professor in Information Systems in both Australia and Qatar. She received the Meritorious Teaching Award from Carnegie Mellon University in 2020 and served as Local Chair of ICIS 2024 in Bangkok. She is the founding president of the Thailand Chapter of the Association for Information Systems and serves on the advisory board for Thailand's national AI policy.
